description: HAVING must be able to evaluate an aggregate that is NOT a SELECT item - it is computed FRESH over each group's rows rather than read back from the already-projected output row. Previously HAVING reused only the SELECT-computed values, keyed by canonical form, so a HAVING aggregate absent from the SELECT resolved to nothing and filtered out every group; the same happened when the SELECT carried it only WRAPPED, as COUNT(*)::VARCHAR while HAVING references bare COUNT(*), because the canonical forms differ. The pre-existing path is guarded too: HAVING on a SELECT alias keeps working, and a predicate mixing a group column with an unselected aggregate resolves both. With no GROUP BY the whole table is one group, and HAVING filters it the same way. Converted 1:1 from query/HavingAggregateResolutionTest (now retired); the fixture's three groups have 2, 1 and 3 rows summing 3, 10 and 12, so no filter can pass by accident.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE t (grp VARCHAR, id INTEGER)
SELECT grp FROM t GROUP BY grp HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ORDER BY grp
CREATE TABLE t (grp VARCHAR, id INTEGER)
SELECT grp FROM t GROUP BY grp HAVING SUM(id) > 5 ORDER BY grp
CREATE TABLE t (grp VARCHAR, id INTEGER)
SELECT grp, COUNT(*)::VARCHAR AS c FROM t GROUP BY grp HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ORDER BY grp
CREATE TABLE t (grp VARCHAR, id INTEGER)
SELECT grp, SUM(id) AS total FROM t GROUP BY grp HAVING total > 5 ORDER BY grp
CREATE TABLE t (grp VARCHAR, id INTEGER)
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t HAVING SUM(id) > 5
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t HAVING SUM(id) > 100
CREATE TABLE t (grp VARCHAR, id INTEGER)
SELECT grp FROM t GROUP BY grp HAVING grp <> 'a' AND COUNT(*) > 1 ORDER BY grp
